Commentary.Commentary: West Indies now have their task cut out and it's safe to say that the writing seems to be on the wall for them. After being on the field for nearly 150 overs, you would expect them to be really tired. A deficit of a massive 386 runs seems like a daunting task but do they have it in them to put up a fight? Will their batsmen show grit and determination or will we see a replica of their first innings? All that for later, first they have to come out and see off around 13 minutes before the lunch break. Don't go anywhere. Stay with us...

There comes the signal from the dressing room - NZ HAVE DECLARED FOR 520/9! If yesterday belonged to Taylor and Colin de Grandhomme, today morning had Tom Blundell written all over it. The debutant made us wait for really long to get to his ton but it was all worth it in the end. Not to forget the effort of Trent Boult at the other end. He offered a stunning hand and dealt with everything that was thrown at him. The duo registered an unbeaten 78-run stand which also happens to be the highest for the 10th wicket for New Zealand against the Windies.
Bowls it wide outside off, Boult lets it be..
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.

NOT OUT! Boult survives yet again! Seeing Trent advancing down the track, Brathwaite fires it outside off and also drags his length back. Boult then tries to camp back to cut but does not connect. The keeper is quick to collect the ball and takes the bails off. The players appeal and the umpire takes it upstairs. Replays show that Boult has planted his back foot inside the crease in time.
Have they finally got Boult out? A stumping appeal has been taken upstairs.
The batsman gets to the pitch of the ball and defends it.
Kraigg Brathwaite is into the attack.
SIX! BANG! Comes down the track, gets to the pitch of the ball and tonks it over the mid-wicket fence. The lead is now 4 runs shy of 390, 400 is what New Zealand is aiming for?
Works it with the spin to mid-wicket.

The local boy becomes the hero of the match, roars Simon Doull on air. Tom Blundell finally gets to his maiden ton in Test cricket, after staying for almost 10 overs in 90s. He does not get there in convincing fashion but who cares. He comes down the track and tries to go big but the ball squirts off the inner half through backward square leg and they take a couple. He screams in joy, takes his helmet off and acknowledges the applause from the crowd. Such a special feeling this would be for the young lad. Well played, Tom! He becomes the fourth wicketkeeper batsman to hit a century on Test debut.
Flatter on off, Tom defends it off the back foot. Three balls to go.
Tosses it up on off, Blundell defends it off the front foot.
Full ball, driven to mid on.
Back of a length on off, Boult defends it. He has done his job, he says over to you Blundell for the next over.

NOT OUT! Missing leg stump! The Windies lose a review. Holder bowls a full toss, which swings in from around off. Boult tries to put bat on ball but misses to get hit on the pads. The Windies appeal but the umpire shakes his head. Holder decides to review and they go upstairs. Replays show that the impact was outside leg. Boult has one ball to survive!
Another review by West Indies for LBW against Boult. It looks like it will be missing leg. A review in hope.
The batsman does well to leave that bouncer.

DROPPED! A tough one but a chance, a definite chance. Holder bowls it on the pads of Boult, he flicks it off the middle but uppishly towards short leg. The fielder there is a little deep, he gets his hands to it, diving to his left but can't hang on. That would have been very unfortunate for both, Boult as well as Blundell had he taken the catch.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot. 4 balls to go.
FOUR! Top shot! Holder dishes out a full ball on off, Trent drives it through mid off for a boundary.

A dot to finish! Works it with the spin towards mid-wicket. Boult is on his bike at the non-striker's end, ready to accelerate but is sent back by Bundell. He remains on 99. Boult will have to survive another over here.
Comes down the track and drives it to mid on. He does not get a single again. Only one ball to go now.
The batsman has driven it through mid on.
Drags his length back on off, Tom pushes it to mid off.
Flatter on off, Blundell defends it off the back foot.
Tosses the ball on off, Tom defends it off the front foot.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman. Trent sees it off again.
Shorter in length on middle, Boult watchfully ducks under it.
Comes around the wicket and lands it on off, Boult guides it to gully.

Blundell wants two but does not get it! Tom flicks it with the angle down towards fine leg. He sets off for the first and calls for the second. But seeing the fielder get to the ball quickly he refuses. He stays on 99, a run away!
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Length on off, Tom defends it off the front foot.
Flatter on off, Boult defends it off the back foot. The crowd gives him a loud cheer as he manages to survive the over. Well done.
Flighted ball on off, Boult defends it onto the ground.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Gives it air on off, Boult lunges forward in defense.
Floats it on off, Boult presses forward and blocks it.
Tosses it up on off, Trent defends it.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot. Tom is in no hurry it seems. He is taking his own time.
Length on off, jags back in. Blundell tries to flick but misses and gets hit high on the pads.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
WIDE! Bouncer which bounces way above the batsman's head and the umpire signals a wide.
Good length on off, Tom defends it.
Short ball on middle, Blundell pulls it down to fine leg.
Length ball outside off, Blundell defends it down safely.

NOT OUT! The impact is umpire's call. Bundell can breath a sigh of relief! Chase tosses it up on off, gets it to drift away. Boult crouches forward and tries to defend it but plays down the wrong line and is struck on the back pad. There is a stifled appeal from the Windies but the umpire stays put. After a while they decide to review. Replays show that there is no bat involved and the impact is umpire's call. Tom would have had his heart in his mouth for a while but there are all smiles around now. West Indies still have their review in tact.
A late review for LBW by West Indies against Boult has been taken. It looks like the drift is taking it away from the off stump.
Floats it outside off, Boult lets it be.
Onto 98! Chase drags his length back on middle, Tom punches it through mid-wicket for a run.
Very full outside off, Blundell tries to guide it towards third man but misses.
Shorter in length on middle, pushes down to long on and Tom refuses to take a single.
Tosses it up on off, driven back to the bowler.
A predetermined defensive shot. Boult already had positioned himself for defending the ball. A full toss on off, Trent blocks it.
Thick inside edge by the batsman, ball goes down to fine leg. The batsmen have run through for a single.
A yorker on off, Tom digs it out.
Okay then, Williamson and co are in whites which indicates they are waiting for Tom Blundell to get to his ton before taking the field...
Lands it on a length around off, Blundell defends it towards point.
Just ahead of a length on off, defended off the front foot.
Length ball outside off, Tom lets it be.

Drinks are on the field. Nothing new to report. The toiling work for the Windies continues as the pair of Blundell and Boult motor along to frustrate them to an extent. They have recorded the highest 10th wicket stand for NZ against WI but all the eyes are on the wicketkeeper. He is just 4 runs away to reach the three-figure mark. Will NZ declare once he gets there? Here comes Jason Holder steaming in.
Eases it down to long on to keep strike in the next over. Tom is just one hit away.
Comes down the track and drives it back towards the bowler.
Floats it outside off, Blundell drives it through extra cover. The fielder at long off runs to his left, dives and saves two for his side.
Flatter on middle, Blundell tries to work it on the leg side but gets a soft leading edge back towards the bowler.
Slower through the air on off, Tom goes for the reverse sweep but mistimes it.
Tosses it up outside off, Tom drives it to covers.
Roston Chase is brought to roll his arm over...
Bumper but down the leg side, Boult lets it be.
Full on the pads, flicked through square leg for a run. 7 runs away now.

500 up for New Zealand! Gabriel bangs it short on Boult's body. Trent somehow manages to fend it away uppishly but as there is no short leg, it lands safely and rolls towards square leg for a run. This is also the highest 10th wicket partnership for New Zealand against the Windies.
Good length outside off, Blundell guides it towards deep point for a run.
Flicks it down to mid on with the angle.
Full toss on the pads, Tom flicks it towards mid on.
Flicks it with the angle on the leg side for a run.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.

FOUR! Into the 90s! Also, this is now the highest score for a Kiwi keeper on debut, beating Ronchi! A short delivery on middle, Blundell does not shy away from a pull, he gets lucky as the top edge flies over the keeper for a boundary.
Full toss on middle, Trent flicks it through mid-wicket for a run.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Sprays it down the leg side, Boult misses the flick.
FOUR! Dismissed! Full and on middle, Bundell drives it straight down the ground to bring up the 50-run stand. New Zealand now lead by 358 runs!
Flicks it with the angle to mid-wicket.
NO BALL! Second of the over. A little bit closer than the last one this time. He lands it on a length around off, defended towards point.
Good length outside off, stays a touch low. Blundell tries to work it down towards third man but gets beaten.
Just ahead of a length outside off, Boult times it through covers for a run.
Fuller in length, driven to mid off.
NO BALL! Gabriel's first of the day! Another one which is way over the line. He bangs it short on off, Boult tries to play the upper cut but misses

Scott Styris tells us something about Trent Boult. He says at the start of this morning he was seen fiddling with the balls outside the line of off stump. Was seen half ducking, half poking which nearly cost him his wicket. But since the moment he played a ramp shot for a biggie his confidence just doubled. He is trying to use the pace, getting his body behind the line as he knows the importance and the hard work of the man at the other end. Yes, Tom Bludell deserves the ton with the way he played and for him to get to that milestone, Boult is equally responsible...
Good length on off, Boult guides it to point.
Fires it down the leg side, Tom tries to flick but misses.
A good yorker on middle, Blundell plays it out equally well.
Good length on off, nipping back in. Blundell tries to defend but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Length, defended off the back foot.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Fuller in length on middle, Blundell flicks it towards deep square leg.
Very full on middle, Boult keeps it out.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Just ahead of a length outside off, Trent tries to cut but gets beaten as the length was not right to play that shot.
Back of a length on off, Boult guides it towards point.
Length outside off, Boult goes for the cut but gets beaten.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.

NOT OUT! Blundell survives! The bounce has saved him there. Holder bowls it on a length on off, gets it to shape in. Blundell walks right across his stump in an attempt to flick. He misses to get hit on the pads. The players appeal but the umpire shakes his head. The ball rolls towards the fine leg fence. Holder reviews it immediately after seeing the umpire signaling it as leg byes. The replays roll in. There is no bat involved and Hawk Eye shows it is just clipping the stumps and hence the on-field call stays. West Indies don't lose a review though! The lead is now above 350.
Shannon Gabriel is into the attack.
Review time! An lbw appeal against Blundell has been given not out. Holder feels he has got his man and he decides to review. He has walked right across, so maybe height could be an issue.
Driven through mid on by the batsman.
Close! Length around off, nips back in sharply. Tom, trusting the bounce makes a leave and the ball just bounces over the off pole.
Bumper on middle, pulled to fine leg.

FOUR! Brilliant effort by Chase but in vain! Holder bowls it shorter in length and outside off this time. Blundell cuts it through backward point. The ball is racing towards the fence, Chase in the deep runs to his left, dives full stretch and tries to push it back in but the ball rolls ahead and touches the ropes.
Short and outside off, a nothing delivery to be honest. Blundell has all the time in the world, to rock back and pull it to the man at deep mid-wicket. He opts against the run though.
Jason Holder brings himself into the attack.
Tom gets the single to retain strike. Roach bowls a slower one on leg stump. Blundell works it to fine leg for a run.
Sweepers coming inside the ring for the last ball of the over...
Fuller in length on middle, Blundell drives it back towards Roach who jumps and stops it with one hand.
Slower ball on off, Tom works it towards square leg with soft hands and takes two. Good running.
Fuller in length outside off, Trent drives it through cover-point for a run.
Full on the stumps, Boult defends it off the front foot.
Length outside off, the batsman lets it be.
Dances down the track and tries to pull the short ball but gets an inside edge onto his pads.

FOUR! Making full use of the field coming in! Blundell comes down the track, gets to the pitch of the ball. The bat turns in his hands as he tries to play the shot but it still goes to the boundary through backward point off the back of the bat.
Fullish ball on off, eased down to mid off.
Just ahead of a length on off, Tom mistimes his drive to mid off.
Good length on off, Blundell guides it to gully.
Full on off, driven crisply but straight to the man at covers.
Fuller on the pads, Boult flicks it through mid-wicket for a brace.
Good length outside off, left alone.
Bowls a bumper on middle, Boult ducks under it.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Good length outside off, Boult first thinks of guiding it down towards third man but then pulls his bat out of the way. Not a smart shot with slips in place.

SIX! All the way! Clever Boult. Roach bangs it in short on off. Boult waits for it and upper cuts it over the slip cordon for a maximum. He loved the shot as he himself was admiring it after playing the shot.
A dot to finish! Length around off, Tom defends it besides the pitch and looks for a run but there ain't any.
Works it with the angle to mid-wicket
FOUR! Into the 70s! Top shot there! This time he cashes in on the width. A full ball outside off, Tom leans into it and drills it through the covers to fetch himself a boundary.
Short and wide outside off, width on offer. Blundell cannot cash in as he goes for the cut but gets beaten. He will be disappointed to not put that away.
Shorter in length outside off, bounces a touch extra. Tom tries to cut but is beaten by the bounce extracted off the surface.
Full ball outside off, Blundell drives it towards deepish mid off but does not run. Holder has pushed his fielder back as he wants Blundell to take a single.
Back of a length on off, defended off the back foot. A maiden but not a threatening one.

Tries bowling a yorker but ends up serving a low full toss on middle. Boult shuffles across and gets his bat down in time and hits it towards fine. He sets off for a run but is sent back by Blundell as he wants strike in the next over.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Poor bowling! Fuller in length outside off, Boult need not play at it. Roach has to attack the stumps.
Bangs it in but outside off, Boult opts not to play at it.
Shorter in length outside off, Trent shuffles across and leaves it.
Kemar Roach will bowl from the other end. He has Trent Boult facing. Can Roach finish it off?
BEATEN! Good finish to the over. Cummins lands it on a length around off, gets it to straighten after pitching. Blundell pokes at it and gets beaten. 10 runs from the over.
FOUR! Not a good first over here by Cummins! He errs in line and bowls it on the pads. Blundell is too good to miss out. He works it down towards the fine leg fence.

A poor start for Cummins, he has not found his lines here. He drifts it on the pads, Tom flicks it very fine towards the fine leg fence. Roach there runs to his right, crouches low and keeps it down to two.
FOUR! Tom started off his innings with a boundary and starts in a similar fashion today. Full length ball on middle, Blundell flicks it past the diving mid on fielder for a boundary.
Good length outside off, Blundell lets it be.
Cummins starts off with a loosener outside off, no pace or zip on that delivery. Blundell who was very watchful yesterday makes a leave.

A bright sunny morning welcomes us here in Wellington. New Zealand ain't declaring. They want the opposition to bowl them out. The umpires and the players make their way out. Tom Blundell will be the man on strike, he will look to score some quick runs. Can he get a ton on debut? Trent Boult will be at the other end. Miguel Cummins will bowl the first over of the day. Here we go...

The Windies on the other hand, still have a wicket to pick before facing the big task. They will look to do that quickly and come out to bat with a positive mindset. Something outrageous is needed if they are to salvage something out of this game. We saw wickets on day 1 and a lot of runs yesterday. What do we have in store today? Will it turn out to be the last day of the Test? We shall find out soon. Stay tuned...

Hello and welcome to day 3 of the first Test between New Zealand and Windies in Wellington. With a lead of 313, the only question here is when will New Zealand declare? Though there is no such pressure on them as there is still a lot of time left in the game. They will look to tire out the West Indian players and hope for the pitch to show some wear and tear before having a crack with the new cherry.
...Day 3, Session 1...

Right, then! The hosts remain on top and it would be interesting to see if they declare overnight or not. The task is cut out for the Windies and it all comes down to their batsmen and how they respond. With three full days to go, a result is certain. Let's see if they can put up a good batting show this time around. Join us for the third day's play tomorrow at 1100 local (2200 GMT) to see if the domination continues. Before we leave, you can catch more Test cricket action from the ongoing Ashes 2nd Test (if it happens) or the third and final Test between India and Sri Lanka by switching tabs. Until then, it's goodbye from us! Have a great weekend!

Well, West Indies would be down and out at the moment. They will be exhausted mentally and physically after being made to toil hard the whole day. If you look at the scorecard, you would see 9 wickets have fallen but the fact is, the batsmen threw it away in an attempt to up the ante. Everyone bowled good in patches but no one looked penetrative enough. They are 313 runs adrift and only a miracle from here can save them.

The Kiwi all-rounder looked fluent as ever the moment he stepped in. It was not all about throwing the bat around but the power and finesse that literally took the game away from the Windies in the blink of an eye. Looking at him, the debutant Tom Blundell joined in the fun and made the most of the tired bodies. The duo blazed a record 148-run stand for the 7th wicket and in the process, broke a few records too. The former registered the second-fastest Test ton for his side while the later became the third Kiwi keeper to have scored a fifty on debut. In the quest to keep scoring, Colin de Grandhomme gifted his wicket away but not before playing a valiant knock.

A day completely dominated by the Kiwis. They amassed 362 runs in the day and have batted the visitors out of the game. Jeet Raval couldn't add much to his overnight total but the veteran, Ross Taylor, continued his love affair with the Windies. He played elegantly alongside Henry Nicholls but departed when he was just 7 short of a ton. It seemed like the Windies might run through the inexperienced middle order but there was one man standing to prove everyone wrong - COLIN DE GRANDHOMME!
Good length outside off, Boult plays inside the line and lets it through to the keeper. THAT WILL BE STUMPS ON DAY 2!
Very full on the stumps, Boult defends it off the front foot.
Bouncer! The batsman tries to upper cut it but misses.
Hits timber but at the other end. Gabriel goes for a yorker but ends up bowling a full toss on the stumps. Boult defends it and the ball rolls and hits the stumps at the non-striker's end.
NO BALL! Gabriel oversteps again and it is a big one. He is way ahead of the line. He bowls a bumper on middle, Blundell pulls it towards fine leg for a run.
Back of a length on off, Blundell defends it off the back foot.
Full and on the stumps. Defended off the front foot.
Gets across, goes low and defends it into the ground.
Edged and away! Floats it up outside off, Boult takes a long stride forward to defend but gets an outside edge which runs past first slip. Two taken.
Boult comes down the track, Chase sees it and fires it full down leg. Trent just manages to get his pad in the way.
Walks across as if he wants to play but then leaves it alone in the end.
Gets down and brooms it down to long leg for a single.
Floated delivery around middle, flicked towards mid-wicket.
Trent Boult is the last man in. 3 overs to go in the day. Can West Indies bowl the Kiwis out?

OUT! Edged and taken! And Gabriel hasn't overstepped this time! He goes wide of the crease and drops it on a length outside off at 133.7 kph. Henry moves leg side and then tries to hang his bat out. The ball takes the feather of the bat and Dowrich behind the stumps accepts it gleefully. Shannon gets his first of the match!
Shortish and outside off, Tom punches it square of the wicket on the off side for a single. Henry comes down the track in search of another which was certainly not on.
Pinged on the pads! That's raw pace! 144.1 kph! This one skids off the surface, Blundell shapes up for the pull but misses and wears it on the pads.
Another yorker outside off, Tom crouches low and with an angled bat he digs it out towards the first slip fielder.
Just missed the off stump! Gabriel fires in a yorker, Blundell tries to keep it out but is late to bring his bat down. Luckily for him the line was outside the off which saves him.
On a length and angling in, Tom with a high bat lift defends it down.
Flatter one on the stumps, blocked off the back foot.
FOUR! Uses the feet and holds the pose too! Delightful! Henry comes down the track to this loopy ball and latches it through mid off to get off the mark.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Comes down the track and almost gets beaten. Somehow manages to push it towards the point fielder.
Floated ball on off, left alone.
Matt Henry is the next man in!

OUT! Bowled 'em! Chase gets his second. What drift he has got here. He lands it around off, Wagner comes forward to defend but the ball skids through, beats the inside edge, kisses the pads and disturbs the timber behind. No real celebration from the Windies. New Zealand lead by 303 runs!
Back of a length on middle and off, Tom Blundell is right back to defend it down.
And Gabriel's perennial problem! He oversteps yet again! Angles it in on a length outside off, defended towards point.
Gabriel spears in a perfect yorker on the stumps, Tom just about manages to keep it at bay.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Goes back to this in-coming delivery and defends.
Fuller and angling in from wide of the crease, Tom Blundell blocks it off the front foot.

FOUR! Inside edge and through! Gabriel angles it into the right-hander, it's not that short but the debutant tries to pull it across the line. Gets an inside edge which just evades the stumps and rolls down to the fine leg fence for a boundary.
More flight outside off, Wagner presses forward in defense.
Leans forward and defends it into the ground.
Loopy outside off, bunted back to Chase.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Goes back and defends this flatter ball back to the bowler.
Tossed up around middle and leg, defended into the leg side.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. The batsmen have run through for a single.

That's a brute of a delivery! Nothing Wagner could do about it. Gabriel bangs in a short ball and it takes off. Wagner doesn't know what to do as he tries to fend this away. Gets hit flush on the gloves as the ball dies down safely. He's getting a taste of his own medicine.
Short and on middle, the batsman ducks.
Good length delivery on leg, glanced fine down the leg side for a couple.
Fuller and angling in, worked towards mid-wicket.
Length ball on middle, defended off the back foot.
Neil Wagner is the new man in. He was just sensational with the ball, can he have fun with the bat?

OUT! An entertaining knock comes to an end! This is the first time Colin de Grandhomme mistimed a shot in otherwise his fluent innings. Chase gives it loop, Colin dances down the track to loft it down the ground but seems to be deceived in the flight. Gets it off the inner half and it goes high up in the air towards long on where Kieran Powell takes an easy catch. The blazing 148-run stand has been broken. Will NZ declare?
Outside off, driven towards cover.
Fifty on debut for Blundell! Becomes the third Kiwi keeper after Baz and Ronchi to achieve this feat. Comes down the track and clips it through mid-wicket for a single.
The batsman dances down the track and does well to block the ball.
Loopy delivery around off, defended off the front foot.
Tossed up outside off, the batsman looks to drive but gets an outside edge which flies past the vacant first slip region. Three runs taken.
Outside off, a play and a miss.
Yorker on middle, jammed out well by Tom.
The batsman has played it to the point region. Spirited effort by the fielder to save runs for his team.

He gets to it! Second fastest Test century for a Kiwi batsman! Well played, Colin de Grandhomme. His maiden in this format. He has literally taken the game away from the Windies here. Takes his helmet off and acknowledges the cheer on offer. Dabs this length delivery through backward point and takes three.
FOUR! Flashes and gets another boundary! Short and wide outside off, Colin de Grandhomme throws his hands at it. Gets an edge that flies over the slip cordon for a boundary. Is on 99 now!
Short and outside off, Tom looks to cut but ends up chopping it in front of point for a single.
Flattish outside off, a steer through point for a single.
Takes a stride ahead and defends it down safely.
Fuller on off, bashed down to long off for one.
Goes back and with the turn clips it behind square on the leg side to collect a couple.

SIX! Into the 90s he goes! This is pure entertainment! Sees the loop, skips down the track does Colin de Grandhomme and lifts it powerfully over long on for a biggie. Will NZ declare once he gets to his ton?
Short and outside off, punched off the back foot towards deep cover for a single.
Fuller and outside off, TB lunges forward and blocks it in front of point to keep strike.
Back of a length outside off, Tom hops back and dabs this on the bounce to Holder at gully.
Fuller and coming back in with the angle, Bludell gets his front foot across, lifts his bat and shoulders his arms.
Once again it's on the shorter length outside off, another slash and a miss by debutant.
Outside off, left alone.
Short and outside off, Blundell looks to flay it through the line but misses.
Fuller and darted around the pads, flicked towards short fine leg where Gabriel dives but couldn't prevent the single.
Goes back to this short ball and flicks it with the spin towards mid-wicket.
Comes forward and blocks it into the ground.
Fuller outside off, drilled once again down to long on for another single.
Dances down the track and milks a single down to long on for one.
Flat and short outside off, punched back to the bowler.
Back of a length outside off, slapped to deep backward point for a single.

FOUR! Bludgeoned! Not even kidding, that's what the debutant has done. Shortish ball, doesn't rise much. Tom Blundell gets it at a good height and thrashes it through mid-wicket for a boundary. 400 up for NZ as well.
Leans ahead and drives it through covers for a single.

Another good shot and it's a no ball too! Cummins has overstepped, West Indies have bowled just too many. Shortish and outside off, slapped uppishly towards third man. Seemed like it would run away but Roach in the deep comes running in to his left and stops it with his left boot. Three running runs is the result.
Similar ball and a similar shot but there are two men in the deep now. So a single results.

FOUR! Booming shot! Cummins drops it short and outside off, Colin de Grandhomme gets on top of it and throws the kitchen sink at it. The ball goes through point and the man in the deep tried his best to stop the ball but comes second best.
Back of a length outside off, a slash and a miss.
Miguel Cummins is brought back into the attack. He was impressive at the start of this session, can he break this stand?
Loopy delivery outside off, defended by coming forward.
Short and outside off, punched down to long on for one.
Wristed down to long on for a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Drifting in from outside off, swiped across the line through mid-wicket for a couple.
Fuller and outside off, blocked off the front foot.
FOUR! Drilled! Fuller in the zone outside off, De Grandhomme absolutely bashes it through extra cover to find the fence. Brings up the 100-run stand as well.
Bangs in a short ball on middle, pulled to deep backward square leg for a single.
Fuller on off, defended off the front foot.
Back of a length outside off, TB dabs it fine down to third man for a couple.
Short and ample of width as well, cut to deep backward point for a single.
Length delivery outside off, easily left alone.
Short ball outside off, de Grandhomme cuts it through point for a run.
Works i with the spin through the leg side for a run.

CAUGHT OFF A NO BALL!  Oh dear, Holder has overstepped. It is the 8th no ball by the Windies in this innings. Poor, very poor just not acceptable by the modern day standards. The second new ball is 16 overs away. Jason Holder will start off the proceedings. He has a slip and a short leg in place. Here we go...

The visitors on the other hand, have looked flat this morning. Agreed, they got a wicket but at the same time they have leaked runs too. Wickets is what they need and they need it in heaps. The sun is out in all its glory and it would require a standout bowling performance on their part to make a comeback. Will they be able to limit the damage or will the toiling work go on? Join us back shortly to see what happens next...

The Kiwis continue to tighten their grip on this Test. They have scored 96 runs in the 26 overs with the loss of a Jeet Raval. Ross Taylor has continued his rich vein of form against the Windies and has already crossed the 50-run mark. He needed good support from the other end and Henry Nicholls didn't let him down. The duo has batted with determination and have shown intent to score whenever there was an opportunity. The current stand is already worth 72 and with the way these two are batting, they are threatening to take the game away from the Windies.
Not an ideal delivery to end the session. Cummins bangs it short but down the leg side. Nicholls moves inside the line to leave it alone. LUNCH ON DAY 2, NZ LEAD BY 47 RUNS!
Comes around the wicket and bowls it on the pads. Nicholls flicks it with the angle through backward square leg to bag a brace.
Short again but down the leg side. The batsman ducks under it.
Back of a length on middle. Nicholls rocks back and defends it.
Shortish ball on middle, Nicholls sways away.
A bumper on middle, Taylor pulls it through backward square leg for a run.
Gives it air outside off, Nicholls drives it to covers.
Very full on middle, the batsman drives it back to the bowler.
Tosses it up on middle, Nicholls drives it to mid on.
Floats it full on off, Nicholls defends it off the front foot.
Flatter outside off, Nicholls pads it away.
Drives the full ball through mid on for a run.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks under the bouncer at the last moment.
Shorter in length down the leg side this time. Nicholls goes for the pull but misses.
Shorter in length outside off, Nicholls tries to pull but does not connect.
NO BALL! Another one by a West Indian bowler! Taylor flicks it through square leg for a run. He now becomes the 26th New Zealand batsman to score 10000 first-class runs.
Good length on off, Taylor defends it off the front foot.
Back of a length on off, Taylor guides it to point.
Bouncer outside off, Taylor tries to drag it on the leg side but gets beaten.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
That was delicately played! Flatter outside off by Chase. Taylor opens the face of the bat and guides it down towards third man for three.
Short and easy for Taylor. He rocks back and cuts it through point for a run.
Plays it with the spin to mid-wicket for a run.
FOUR! Streaky! Tosses it up outside off, Taylor tries to drive it through the off side, against the spin. The ball takes the outside edge and goes through short third man for a boundary.
Fires it on leg stump, spinning down the leg side. Taylor tries to flick but misses.
Back of a length on middle, Nicholls defends it off the back foot.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.
NO BALL! Cummins oversteps this time! He bowls it short on middle, Taylor pulls it through square leg for a run.
Back of a length on off, Taylor defends it off the back foot.
Some chin music for the batsman, he lets that bouncer through to the wicketkeeper.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
How do you play that? He bowls it fuller on off, gets it to shape away after pitching. Taylor tries to drive but is beaten.
Floats it on off, the batsman defends it off the front foot.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Lunges forward and blocks it down into the ground.
Gives it air on off, the batsman defends it off the front foot.
Pushes through quicker on off, Raval pushes it to covers.
Tosses it up on middle, the batsman defends it off the front foot.
Change of ends for Roston Chase.
FOUR! Not convincing but Taylor won't mind! Cummins bangs it in short on middle. Ross goes the pull but gets a top edge over the keeper for a boundary.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Good length on off, Taylor defends it watchfully.
Short, pulled towards square leg for a run.
Back of a length on off, Latham defends it towrads point.
Good length on off, the batsman need not play a it.
Miguel Cummins is back into the attack.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman.

FOUR! Fifty for Taylor! No. 28 for him. He loves playing against Windies, doesn't he? Shannon bangs it in short on middle. Taylor pulls it through backward square leg for a boundary. He acknowledges the applause from the crowd. This also brings up the 50-run stand in only 60 balls. A very entertaining partnership.
Flicks it to mid-wicket with the angle.
Bowls it down the leg, the batsman flicks it down to fine leg for a run.
The ball is way outside the off stump, easy leave for the batsman.
Full outside off, Taylor square drives it for a run. The lead is now 20.
Flatter on off, defended solidly.

Tosses it up on off, defended off the front foot.
Fires it down the leg side, Nicholls misses the flick.
Time for spin! Roston Chase is into the attack.
On the pads, too easy for Nicholls. He flicks it through square leg for three.
The short of length delivery has been cut away through square on the off side. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Fullish on off, Taylor drives it towards cover where the fielder misfields and concedes two.

WOW! That took off from a length! Taylor can do nothing but only smile but that was very well played by the veteran. Gabriel bowls it on off, the ball bounces off the surface. Takes Taylor by surprise who hops but does well to drop his wrists down in time.
NO BALL! Second of the over, maybe the wind behind his back is forcing him to overstep. He again lands it on  a length around off, The batsman tries to defend but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Fuller on off, Taylor drives it to mid off.
NO BALL! Gabriel and overstepping seems to go hand in hand. A big one too. He lands it on a length around off, jags back in. Taylor tries to play it but misses to get hit on the pads.
A short ball on middle, Taylor ducks under it.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Errs in line and bowls it on the pads, Nicholls flicks it down to fine leg for a brace.

Simon Doull on-air mentions that he has observed Henry Nicholls getting out chopping onto the stumps very often. He should be avoiding the balls outside off as he is new to the crease. Given that the pacers are getting the extra bounce on this surface, can prove fatal if he tries to fiddle with the wide one...
The batsman has punched the ball off the backfoot. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Comes around the wicket and sprays it on the pads. Nicholls flicks it down to fine leg for a run.
Flicks it with thr angle towards square leg for a run.
BEATEN! Gabriel lands it on a length around off, gets it to shape away after pitching. Nicholls hangs his bat out needlessly only to get beaten.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Back of a length on off, Nicholls defends it to point.
Lengh ball around leg, shapes in. Nicholls tries to flick but misses and gets hit on the pads. The players appeal but the umpire remains put. Missing leg probably.
Back of a length on off, Nicholls defends it easily.
Fullish ball on off, Taylor drives it to mid off for a run.

Drinks! It's been a good hour of play for the hosts. They lost Raval but they have gotten into the lead too. Ross Taylor is looking set and scoring runs at will. He certainly will be eyeing a big one. West Indies would feel if they get Taylor out quickly, there might be chances of limiting the damage as the hosts' middle order is inexperienced. Let's see how they fare till the lunch break...
Lands it on a length outside off, the batsman again does not play at it.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
Fullish on off, the batsman is not interested to play at it.
Full and wide outside off, Nicholls lets it be.
The Kiwis are now into the lead by just a run though. Works it around the corner, with the angle for an easy run.
Fullish ball on off, Nicholls defends it onto th ground.
FOUR! SCORES LEVEL! What timing! Shannon bowls it on the pads, the batsman flicks it through square leg for a boundary. 9 runs from the over so far.
Full ball on off, Nicholls defends off the front foot.
Flicks it with the angle towards square leg for a run.
FOUR! DEFT! Finds that gap nicely. Shortish ball outside off. Taylor guides it between gully and second slip for a boundary.
Short of a length outside off, comes in with the angle. Too close for the batsman to cut. Taylor still goes through with the shot but gets beaten.
Shannon Gabriel is into the attack.
Just ahead of a length outside off, the batsman shoulders his arms to it.
Bowls it on  a length around off, Raval leaves it.
Length outside off, Nicholls does not play at it.
The batsman defends it from within the crease. They pick up a single.
FOUR! Again, he is guilty of overpitching here. Almost a carbon copy of the last shot. A similar line and length outside off. Taylor drives it through covers this time for a boundary.
FOUR! Too easy, not learning here the Windies bowler. They again dish out a full ball outside off, Taylor leans into it and drives it through extra cover for a boundary.
Back of a length on off, Nicholls defends it back to the bowler.
Shortish on middle, Nicholls gets over the bounce and pulls it down to the fielder at square leg.
Length outside off, the batsman is not interested at playing at it.
Back of a length on off, Nicholls defends it to point.
He changes the angle again and comes over the wicket! Short and wide outside off, Nicholls tries to cut but gets beaten.
From around the wicket he lands it around off. The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Good length on off, Taylor defends it off the front foot.
The batsman guides it to third man.
Fullish ball outside off, easy for Taylor. He drives it through covers for a couple.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat. One run added to the total.
FOUR! Off the mark in style but not convincingly! Short and on the body, Nicholls tries to pull but gets a top edge over backward square leg for a boundary.
Henry Nicholls is the next man in!

OUT!  Ian Bishop on air did mention there was a need for a bowling change and it has reaped huge dividends instantly. Roach gets the breakthrough. He comes steaming in from over the wicket and lands it on a length around off, gets it to shape away. The line is such that Raval has to play at it. He gets a thin outside edge as he tries to defend. It goes to the keeper who pouches it. The players appeal and the umpire raises his finger. The Windies are ecstatic. A gritty knock from Raval comes to an end. New Zealand now trail by 25 runs.
There's the first change of the morning. Kemar Roach is into the attack.
The batsman has pushed it to the cover region.

Good point from Ian Bishop. He says if you are bowling according to the plan then you need to set the field accordingly. Holder is persisting with the short ball and is bowling it right on the money. But what he has done is he has placed a short leg a bit deep and a gully too is not at its usual position. They need to come in closer to stand a chance...

The ploy almost paid off! Holder bangs it in short on middle, the ball skids off the surface and also gets big on the batsman. Taylor blindly tries to defend it off the back foot but the ball lobs off his glove but lands short of gully. Holder is frustrated as nothing is going his way.
Back of a length on middle, Taylor defends it.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Back of a length on middle, Taylor defends it off the back foot.

A change in angle he comes around the wicket to the right-hander. He bowls it on a length around middle. Taylor might have been expecting a bouncer and is hence, late on the flick and is hit high on the thigh pad.
Bowls it on middle, Taylor with soft hands, plays it towards mid-wicket for a brisk single.
Back of a length on off, Taylor defends it off the back foot.
Flicks it with the angle down to fine leg for a run.
Back of a length on middle, Raval defends it off the back foot.

Tucks it with the angle to mid-wicket.

Length outside off, Ross opts not to play at it.
Bouncer! The batsman does well to evade it.
Length on off, Taylor defends it off the back foot.

The Windies have gone defensive today morning. They have only one slip. The commentators feel the end from which Holder is bowling is the end to take wickets from. As from the other end you are bowling into the wind, which is relatively tough.
Good length on off, Taylor defends it off the front foot.
Shortish ball outside off, Taylor cuts it towards gully. The fielder there dives to his right and makes a good stop.
Bouncer on middle, Raval ducks under it.

Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.

Raval throughout his innings has not looked comfortable against the short ball. Cummins bowls a bouncer, a well-directed one. The ball zips off the surface. Raval is late in the pull and the ball hits him on the glove and rolls towards square leg.
Very full ball on middle, Taylor flicks it to fine leg for a run. That also brings up the 100. They now only trail by another 34.
Good length on off, Taylor defends it off the back foot.
Fullish on off, Taylor drives it through covers. The fielder from mid off gives it a chase and stops the ball inside the ropes. The batsmen run three.

Brilliant by Gabriel! Full and on middle, Taylor flicks it towards mid on. The big, fast bowler there dives to his right and makes a very good stop. He also scores a direct hit at the non-striker's end but the batsman did not leave his crease. He saved four runs for his side there.
Lovely length here by Holder around off, Taylor defends it solidly.
Length ball around off, Taylor defends it to point.

Simon Doull on-air feels that Mitchell Santner is being wasted down at no. 6 as according to him he is a very talented cricketer. He should be playing a lot more first-class cricket, work on his batting and get among the runs to be promoted up the order.

Length outside off, Taylor lets it be.
Flicks it through square leg for a run.

Just ahead of a length outside off, Raval lets it be and the ball goes on the bounce to the keeper.
Good length outside off, angling away. Left alone by the batsman.
Angles it into the pads, Taylor flicks it through square leg for a run.

Simon Doull on-air has got something to say. He says Miguel Cummins bowled a nasty bouncer on the last ball of day 1 to surprise Ross Taylor. He further says that, the last time Morne Morkel bowled one to him, he broke his arm and Taylor was out injured. The point here is that, you need to keep hitting those areas to trouble the batsman. Today, the very first ball that Ross faced was a genuine half-volley which he easily caressed through the cover region. This will only help his cause and ooze his confidence...
Miguel Cummins will bowl from the other end.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
FOUR! ELEGANT! Full and on off, Raval presses forward and drives it through mid off to fetch the first boundary of the day.
Fuller in length on off, Raval drives it to mid off.
Taylor is underway with three! Full and outside off, Taylor drives it through covers. The fielder gives it a chase and saves a run for his side.
Bowls it on the pads, Raval tucks it towards mid-wicket for a run. First run for the Kiwis today.

Edged but just short! Would have been an ideal start for West Indies. Holder starts right on the money, on a length around middle, nips away after pitching. Raval tries to defend but is undone by the extra bounce. The ball takes the outside edge and falls just short of gully.

We are ready to get underway on day 2. The men who matter make their way out to the middle. Jeet Raval and Ross Taylor will resume their innings. Jason Holder will start the proceedings for West Indies. He was excellent yesterday. Can he strike early? He has two slips and a gully in place.

The away side on the other hand, need to make early inroads if they are to get back into the game. A lot will depend on their pacers who were wayward at the start yesterday, but later did really well to get back into the rhythm. We saw 12 wickets to fall on day 1 and with the pitch expected to spice up today, what do we have in store? Will we see something similar or will it be a run-fest today? Be it anything, we welcome you to the coverage of the second day's  play between New Zealand and Windies in Wellington. Stay with us as the action is about to resume...

We head into day 2 with the hosts sitting comfortably in the driver's seat after a brilliant bowling performance by Wagner. They now just trail by 49 runs and have 8 wickets in hand. Jeet Raval who is now set, after facing over a hundred balls, has an experienced Ross Taylor for company. The pair will look to stay for as long as possible to bat the Windies out of the game. They need to as their middle order is a bit fragile and an early wicket this morning could hamper their chances to take a big lead.
...Day 2, Session 1...

Right then! The Kiwis are right on top at the moment and a sensible batting performance will see them stamping the authority further on this Test. Do the Windies have it in them to make a comeback or will they be made to toil on day 2? We shall find out tomorrow when we meet at 1100 LOCAL (2200 GMT). Until then, goodbye and take care.

Meanwhile, NEIL WAGNER is up for an interview with Simon Doull. He says he is really elated with his efforts with the ball today. Agrees that there were a few funny dismissals which went his way. Apart from that he stuck to his plan and feels happy about it. Further says, the breeze was quite stiff and there wasn't any swing on offer which made him and Boult to hit the deck hard to force a result. Laughs and says it's very tough to keep the short ball stuff going. Says hitting the gym is the key to his success as fitness plays an important role. On he being padded up as the nightwatchman, he says he wants to chip in with the bat too. On the pitch, he reckons, on day 1, it's a bit on the slower side but quickens up as the game progresses.

Jason Holder, then along with Miguel Cummins provided some relief in the dressing room. In the final passage of play in the third session, both bowled with a lot of heart, were disciplined enough and made the batsmen fall into the prey. Eventually, the skipper got the breakthrough while it was his smart captaincy that got the better of his opposite number. Raval has looked a bit fidgety but he has been there for a long time. Taylor has just stepped in and it would be interesting to see if he can do what he did against the Windies when he had them here last time.

Wagner and Boult, both stuck to the short ball ploy and reaped huge dividends. The former registered his career-best figures by picking up a 7-fer while the latter got two to his name as the hosts bundled out the Windies for a scanty 134. Now, all the eyes were on the visitors as to how will they come out to bowl. They had to make the new ball count and to their dismay, they didn't live upto it at all. They sprayed all around the pads which let the Kiwi openers get into the flow.

What a day of Test match we got to witness! On a green pitch, Kane Williamson opted to have a go with the cherry first and his decision almost looked like a wrong one as Powell and Brathwaite looked solid as a rock until the first drinks break. God knows what happened or what words were exchanged by the skipper, all of a sudden there was an inspiring display of bowling performance. Neil Wagner, the destroyer-in-chief, brought in his barrage of short stuff to dismantle the brittle-looking batting line-up.
What a way to end the day! It stung Taylor right on the left fore-arm who took his eyes off the ball in trying to fend it away. STUMPS ON DAY 1, NZ TRAIL BY 49 RUNS!
Bangs in a short ball on middle, Taylor ducks to let that one sail over him to the keeper.

A shout for an LBW, nothing from the umpire. Bowls a skiddy length delivery outside off, this comes back in after pitching. Taylor doesn't account for the inward movement and gets struck on the pads. They appeal but the impact seemed to be outside the line and the height was also an issue.
Takes a stride forward to this length delivery and defends it down.
Drops it on a length outside off, it holds its line too. Ross Taylor makes a watchful leave.
Angles it in from outside off, Taylor blocks it back down the wicket.
After the end of the over, Rod Tucker has a look at his watch, there is still a minute to go. Which means this should be the last over of the day. Can West Indies pick another one?
In the channel outside off, left alone by the southpaw.
And now a no ball! He oversteps and will have to reload. Fuller in length on middle and leg, flicked towards square leg for a single.
Fuller in length and at the base of off stump, Taylor looks to drive but mistimes it towards mid off.
Angles it in from outside off, blocked by coming forward.

A delay here. Already we will get a few overs less today and then there is a sightscreen issue now. The end from which Gabriel is bowling pre-dominantly has this problem, says Ian Smith on air. The issue is that the sightscreen at this end is at a slightly lower height than the one at the other end. So when the bowler comes in with a high-arm action, it offers a hindrance to the batsmen.
Angles it down leg, Taylor tries to help it on its way but misses out. Gabriel has been a bit too erratic in this spell.
Sprays it full and on the pads, wristed behind square on the leg side for a single.
Slants it across the left-hander, Jeet Raval shoulders his arms to that one.
Good length delivery on middle, tucked towards the fielder at mid on.
Fuller in length on off, a front foot push that finds the fielder at cover.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

A stifled appeal! This one nips back in from a length outside off, Taylor is beaten by the in-ward movement and is hit on the pads. They appeal but the umpire stays put. The impact was outside the line.
On a back of a length, angling in, defended solidly off the front foot.
On a length and outside off, Ross Taylor offers his defensive skills.
Miguel Cummins to have a burst before the close of play...
Fuller and a bit too straight on the stumps, clipped through mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Gabriel hits the deck hard, gets a good amount of bounce but it's too high to worry the batsman.
Fuller in length on off, stroked towards the mid off fielder.
Back of a length on middle Raval rises to tap it towards the cover region.
Fuller in length and slanted just outside off, Raval is in two minds whether to go after it or to leave it alone. In the end has a tentative poke at it only to get beaten.
Stays put to this length ball and defends it down.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Works it fine off the pads down the leg side for a brace.
Taylor wants to go at everything here. This time he shapes up for a pull shot but the length is not an ideal one. The ball sneaks under his bat and settles into the gloves off the keeper.

FOUR! That's thrashed! Ross Taylor has flayed this one through the line. This time he gets the width, gets on top of the bounce and unfurls a cracking square cut off the middle of the bat through point for a boundary.
Short of a length delivery on off but doesn't offer enough width. Taylor opts to cut it away but gets cramped for room. Ends up chopping it towards gully.
Length delivery on middle, Taylor looks to pack a punch down the ground but ends up mistiming it back to the bowler.
Touch fuller on middle and off, driven back to the bowler who crouches low in his followthrough to stop it.
This time Taylor waits for the short ball and with soft hands, works it in front of square on the leg side for a single.
Short stuff from Shannon, it's near the rib cage, Raval hops a touch and tucks it behind square on the leg side for a single.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks in time to let that one go over him.
Goes over the wicket, drops it on a back of a length on middle. Dealt with a straight bat.
Sprays it down the leg side, Raval looks to help it on its way but fails to get any wood on that one. Lucky Gabriel to have gotten away with that one.
The batsman has driven that ball straight back.
Short ball but it doesn't rise much. Ross pulls it off the meat of the bat but the man at short mid-wicket dives full length to his right to save a certain boundary.
Back of a length on middle, Taylor stands tall to keep it out.
FOUR! Cracked it away! Short and a bit wide outside off, Ross senses an opportunity to score as he flays it behind square on the leg side for a boundary.
Spills one down leg, Taylor looks to flick it away but gets beaten.

Beware of Ross Taylor! The last time West Indies toured New Zealand, this man was in firing form. He scored a double ton, followed by a couple of hundreds. Shows how important this wicket would be for the Windies...
Fuller in length on off, pushed towards the cover region.
Works it off the back foot towards mid-wicket.
Stands tall and defends it from within the crease.

Ahead of a length outside off, JR lunges forward and offers a straight blade.

On a length and it comes back in a bit, Raval prods forward and defends it right under his nose.
Shannon Gabriel is brought back into the attack.
Brings the sucker ball into play, keeps it full on off. Ross drives it back to the bowler. A wicket maiden for Roach!
Short but the line is outside the off stump, Taylor once again sits down.
Bangs in a short ball on middle, Taylor ducks under the bumper. A good welcome by Roach.
Ross Taylor is the new man in. He has a lot of experience. Can he make it count?

OUT! Straight to the man at gully. Kemar Roach is all pumped up as he knows the importance of this wicket of the skipper, Williamson who stands there in disbelief! Got to give credit to Holder here for keeping two gullies for his opposite number. Roach bowls it short, it's wide too and Kane decides to cash in on it. Cuts it hard but doesn't bother to keep it down. Flies straight to Shai Hope at widish gully who takes a good catch. Williamson walks back for a cheap score and his side trails by 66 runs.
This one keeps coming in from a length outside off. Williamson takes his front foot across the line, knows where is off stump is and then leaves it alone.

Very well bowled! He bowls it on a length around off, angling into the batsman first and then leaves him. Raval first thinks of playing it but then plays inside the line and takes his bat out of the way.
Good length outside off, coming in with the angle. Raval does not fiddle with it.

Back of a length on off, pushes towards cover for a quick single.
Flicks it with the angle to mid-wicket.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
Bowls it wide outside off, Raval does not play at it.
Top edge which goes high in the air...but falls safe! Shorter in length on middle, Raval tries to pull but he gets a top edge which falls in no man's land towards deep square leg for a couple.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Good length outside off, Raval need not play at it.
Length outside off, Raval lets it be.
Kemar Roach is back into the attack.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Back of a length on off, Williamson guides it to point.
A quick bouncer! That really had a lot of fizz behind it. It was on middle, Williamson at the very last moment sways away.
Good length on off, Williamson defends it off the front foot.
Kane Williamson strides out to the middle.

OUT! The skipper provides the much-needed breakthrough. He deserved this wicket. He has bowled brilliantly to both the batsmen. Latham's luck has finally ran out and he too like many other batsmen today has fallen prey to the short ball. Holder bangs it in from around the wicket on middle. Latham tries to pull it but is undone by the bounce and he balloons an easy catch to Roach at mid on. The 65-run stand has been broken. A similar time when the Windies lost their first but can the visitors build on this? New Zealand trail by 69 now.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
FOUR! This time he plays it well! Once again he goes for the paddle and this time he connects it fine down the leg side for a boundary.
Tosses it up outside off, Raval lets it be.
Wide outside off, the batsman need not play at it.
Raval wants the helmet to be changed. Maybe, there was a dent.
Premeditation there by Raval! Not smart by the left-hander. Chase bowls it outside off, Raval goes down early to play the paddle sweep but the ball hits the top edge and goes onto his helmet.
Tosses it up on off, Raval drives it to covers.
Bowls it on a length around off, Latham defends it off the front foot.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.

Almost chops it on! Nothing is going the Windies' way. Holder bowls it short outside off, Latham tries to cut but gets a bottom edge which bounces very close to the off pole and then rolls on the bounce to the keeper.
Length around off, shapes into the batsman. Latham tries to defend it but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Good length outside off, comes back in a touch. Latham trusts the bounce and lets it be.
Quicker outside off, goes on with the arm. Raval watchfully makes a good leave.
Fuller on off, driven to covers.
Slower through the air on off, turning away. Raval, at the very last minute opens the face of the bat and guides it through short third man for a couple.
Flatter on middle, Raval defends it off the front foot.
Short and outside off, Raval looks to go after it but fails to get going with the shot. The ball bounces a touch more and hence Raval is beaten.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.

Drinks! The Kiwis continue their domination so far. Both the openers have gotten their eye in and have slowly increased the scoring rate as well. In the last half an hour, Holder and Cummins have posed a few questions and troubled both the batsmen. Latham was even given a life by Dowrich when he was on 31. So, 19 overs are remaining in the day, will West Indies strike before the close of play? Okay then, time for spin for the first time today. ROSTON CHASE to roll his arm over. Is it because with the two southpaws out there?
Beaten! Back of a length around middle, some extra bounce as well. Raval looks to have a tentative poke at it inside the line which nearly beats the outside edge of his bat.
Back of a length delivery outside off, third leave in a row.
Back of a length in the zone outside off, JR doesn't offer any shot.
On a length and hurled outside off, Jeet makes an easy leave.
Short of a length delivery outside off, Raval ducks to evade it.
Shortish around middle, defended by shuffling across towards mid-wicket.
Gets across to this length ball outside off and at the last moment pulls his bat out to make a leave.
Shortish around leg, tucked towards square leg.

This is a good one! Bowls it on a length, very close to the off stump line and more importantly making the batsman play at it. Latham has a poke at it and it nearly takes the outside edge of his bat to the keeper.
Fuller and wider outside off, TL has got nothing to do with that one.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Back of a length on middle, tapped off the back foot towards mid-wicket.
Holder needs to make the batsman play, he once again hurls it wider in the channel outside off. Easily left alone again. After such a fruitful previous over, Holder bowls an ordinary one.
Bowled wider outside off, no shot offered.
Length delivery on the hips, tucked gently behind square on the leg side for a single.
Short of a length delivery on middle, takes Tom by surprise who goes back and awkwardly fends it away towards the vacant short leg region.
Once again Tom shoulders arms to let that one through.
Fuller and angling away wide outside off, Latham finally realizes that he shouldn't be playing at those.
Stands tall and taps this back of a length delivery towards mid-wicket for a single.
Length delivery, but a bit too straight from the bowler. TL gets across and tucks it behind square on the leg side for a brace.
FOUR BYES! But boy, that shoots off the deck. Miguel bangs in a short ball around leg, Latham looks to pull but it flies off the deck and over a leaping Dowrich behind to the boundary.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Latham is falling into the trap here! Maybe, a lapse in concentration? Cummins once again offers width and asks the batsman to go after it. Tom obliges and is beaten all ends up again.
A bit wider outside off, Latham tires to go at it with hard hands but the ball goes under his bat and settles into the gloves off the keeper.
Short of a length delivery outside off, Jeet Raval isn't interested in playing that.
Brilliant from the skipper again! He once again drops it on a length and gets it to nip away. Jeet has a poke at and is lucky to not edge one.

FOUR! That's gone through again! Both Raval and Latham are lucky to get away. Holder goes full and sprays it outside off. Raval sans any foot movement tries to drive it away. Gets a thick outside edge which flies right past the gully fielder for a streaky boundary. 50 comes up for the Kiwis!
Outside off, left alone.
Back of a length outside off, Jeet plays inside the line to get beaten.

Inside edge... dropped! Dowrich tries his best to take it but the ball doesn't stick. Ahhh, tough! Holder bowls it on a length around off, it comes back in a touch. Latham has a poke at it but gets an inside edge over the stumps and it flies behind. Dowrich dives full length to his right to take it with his right hand but fails to cling onto that one. A chance goes down. And they even steal a run.
Shortens his length but slants it wider outside off, easily left alone.
Slightly fuller this time around middle and off, blocked solidly off the front foot.
Drops it on a back of a length on middle, JR rises on his toes and with a straight bat defends it back to Cummins.
Keeps it away on a length outside off, the batsman stands put to let the keeper do the job.
Brings it back into Jeet who goes back to tuck it away but gets an inside edge on the thigh pad as the ball rolls towards cover.
Cummins hits the deck hard but this one bounces too high. Raval calmly ducks under it. The umpire calls it one for the over.
Full ball outside off, Latham lets it be.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
FOUR! Too easy, this one! Short and wide outside off, Latham's eyes light up as he sees the width. He gets up on the toes cuts it over the man at backward point for another boundary.
Bouncer! The batsman does well to evade it.
FOUR! That was not totally controlled, it was in the air for a while but the placement was good. Shorter in length outside off, Latham guides it uppishly through backward point for a boundary.
Wide enough outside the batsman need not play at it.
Back of a length on off, Tom defends it towards covers.

Cut him into two halves! Cummins lands it on a length around off, gets it to shape back in. Raval tries to force it through the leg side but is beaten on the inside. Good bowling from Miguel is causing some trouble for both the batsmen.
Good length outside off, Raval shoulders his arms to it.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Back of a length on off, Raval pushes it to covers.

Another appeal but the umpire shakes his head again! Shorter in length around middle, stays down a touch. Raval tries to pull but the ball goes off something to the keeper who appeals after taking it. The umpire shakes his head. After a long thought, Holder decides against the review. A smart move by Holder as replays show it had flicked the flap of the pad and not the bat. A good decision by the umpire too.
Shorter in length outside off, Latham pushes it to point.
Good length on middle, Tom pushes it back to the bowler.
Bowls it on a length outside off, Latham lets it be.
Lands it around off, angling away. Latham does not fiddle with it.
Back of a length on middle, Tom defends it off the back foot.
Shortish outside off, Latham chops it to the keeper.
Bangs it in short on middle, Raval comfortably pulls it through backward square leg for a brace.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Outside off, on a length. Raval shoulders his arms to it.
Shorter in length on leg stump, Raval goes for the pull but is late on it and gets hit high on the thigh pad.
Shorter in length outside off, Raval cuts it to the man at gully.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
Good length outside off, Latham lets it be.

FOUR! A lovely reply to the last delivery by Latham. He gets a full ball outside off, a half-volley. Latham leans into it and drives it through covers for a boundary. The deficit is now less than 100.
WOW! A ripper! That has gone a long way off the pitch. Holder lands it around middle and leg. The ball nips away after pitching. Latham tries to drive but is beaten by the movement.
Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone.
Good length on off, Latham defends it off the front foot.

He immediately troubles Latham with the extra bounce, something that Ian Bishop was talking about a while back. Jason lands it just behind a length outside off, the ball bounces a bit extra off the surface. Latham tries to cut it through the off side but gets beaten. There is a muted appeal from the players but the umpire shakes his head.
Jason Holder brings himself into the attack. Can the skipper lead from the front? Two slips and a gully for him...
Full outside off, Raval drives it through covers for a brace.
Flicks it off his pads through the leg side for a run.
Back of a length on off, Raval plays it towards point to change strike.

FOUR! They are playing the short balls with ease, something the Windies could not do. Shortish in length on middle, Raval gets on top of the bounce and pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary. The secret of playing the short ball is to get on top of it, something that the visitors lacked considerably. But one can argue that Wagner had bowled with a lot of venom behind it and to replicate that, the Windies' bowlers need to really steam in.
Length on off, the batsman drives it towards mid on and sets off for a run. The fielder there gets to the ball and has a shy at the non-striker's end but misses. A run added to the total.
Good length on off, Latham defends it towards covers.
Shortish on off, Latham taps it towards covers for a run.
Shorter in length on off, Latham guides it to point.
Wide enough for the batsman to play at it.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
FOUR! Crunched! Short and on middle, Latham swivels inside the crease and pulls it through square leg for a boundary.
Back of a length on off, Latham defends it off the back foot.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Shortish on middle, Raval is solid in defense.
Full ball on off, Raval drives it to mid off.
Back of a length on off, Raval defends it off the back foot.

The commentators on-air feel Jason Holder should bring himself into the attack early. He's tall and can get that extra bounce off the surface which can cause trouble to the batsmen. There is no seam and swing on offer and the bowlers need to bend their backs to get rewards.
Length outside off, Raval lets it be.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

Misunderstanding between the two but no harm done! Back of a length on off by Gabriel. Latham taps it towards cover and wants a run but is sent back by his partner. The fielder gets to the ball but Latham is quick to make his way back.
Back of a length on off, Latham guides it to point.
Bouncer! Latham leaves it alone.
No ball! His first and it was well and truly over the line. A nasty ball on middle, gets big on the batsman. Latham fends it towards mid-wicket.
Back of a length on middle, Tom defends it towards mid-wicket.
Length outside off, Latham does not fiddle with it.
Driven through mid off by the batsman.
Fullish on off, Raval drives it to mid off.

Was there an edge? Roach certainly feels so but the umpire does not. He bangs it short down the leg side. Raval goes for the pull but he seems to have missed it. The keeper collects the ball and he along with Roach appeals but the umpire shakes his head. Replays show it was a good cal from the umpire.
Lands it full outside off, Raval drives it to mid off.

Ian Bishop on-air informs us that the reason why Kemar Roach has gone around the wicket for Raval is that - In the warm-up game against New Zealand A he bowled it from that angle and kept the length not fully overpitched nor short either. It made Raval driving him through the line which induced an edge to the slip cordon. Maybe, he is trying something similar again today...
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Length outside off, Raval lets it be.
FOUR! Short and wide and it has been sent away to the fence. Gabriel provides width to Latham, just where he likes it. He cuts it through point for a boundary. 7 from the first over after the break.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Bangs it in on middle, Latham flicks it through square leg for a brace.
Fullish length outside off, Latham makes a leave.
Shorter and wider outside off, the batsman opts not to play at it.
A run off the first ball after the break! Good length on off, Raval taps it towards mid off for a brisk single.

We are back for the final session. 36 overs are still left in the day. It has been a day full of wickets tumbling. Will the plot remain the same? Well, West Indies will surely be hoping for that to happen. Shannon Gabriel will bowl the first over after the break. For New Zealand, Tom Latham and Jeet Raval will continue their innings. Here we go...

So, after steamrolling the West Indian batting line-up, the two Kiwi openers have negotiated the tricky period before tea really well. They would look to pile up more runs after the break as the wicket is also getting easier to bat on. The Windies on the other hand, have bowled a bit too far outside off. They will need to make the new ball count by landing it in the right areas to make the batsmen play. Early wickets is the need of the hour for them. Can they come out all guns blazing and do what Wagner did to them earlier or will it be the other way round? Join us for the third and final session of the day in a while...
Finishes the session off with a bouncer but outside off. Latham evades it. TEA ON DAY 1!

Loose, very loose. Not a shot you want to be playing in the last over before lunch. Cummins throws it wide outside off, Latham tries to force it through the off side but away from his body and he gets beaten.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks in time to let that one go over him.
Shorter outside off, Latham leaves it.

Poor from the Windies. They don't have a lot of runs in the bag and such silly errors is just not acceptable. Cummins bangs it a touch short around off. Raval first thinks of playing at it but then tries to leave it. The ball came quickly and hits his bat. It goes towards gully where the fielder misfields and concedes a run.
Length outside off, the batsman lets it be.
Miguel Cummins is into the attack now. He will probably bowl the last over before tea.
Drops it on a length just outside off, Latham looks to shoulder his arms but this one comes back in just a shade and goes over the off stump. A maiden for Shannon!
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Slants it away outside off, no shot offered.

Everyone in the cricketing world knows that Gabriel has no ball issues. After bowling the previous delivery, Shannon was seen looking at the landing area so Simon Doull quips by saying that he is making sure that he doesn't overstep today or in this innings...
Lands it on a length outside off, Latham carefully watches it go through to the keeper.
Another short ball, angling away outside off at a good pace. TL arches back to evade it. A good take from Dowrich too.
Gabriel runs in hard, bends his back and gets the extra bounce. Latham easily ducks under it as it was too high.
Shorter in length around off, Raval lets it be.
Off the back foot this time! Shorter in length around off, Latham punches it through covers. Chase gives it a chase and picks it up before it crosses rope. The batsmen in the meantime run three.
Full outside off, Latham drives it through covers. The fielder from point hares after it and keeps it down to two.
Better! Back of a length on off, Latham defends it towards point for a run.
Fuller in length outside off, Raval does not play at it. Roach has to make the batsman play a lot more. He had the same problem in England where he kept bowling wide outside off.
Back of a length but outside off, left alone.
Good length on middle, defended solidly.
Shortish length on leg stump, Latham flicks it towards backward square leg for a run.
Back of a length angling away from the batsman. Raval shoulders his arms to it.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Just ahead of a length on middle, defended solidly.
Fullish ball outside off, Raval keeps his eyes on the ball and makes a leave.
Length ball outside off, Latham opts not to fiddle with it. A maiden by Roach, not a threatening one though.
In the zone outside off, Latham watchfully does not play at it.
That zipped off the surface! Roach lands it on a length around middle, it angles into the batsman. Latham tries to clip it but misses to get hit on the thigh pad.
Back of a length on off, Tom defends it towards point off the back foot.
Wider outside off, Latham leaves it.
Comes around the wicket and bowls it outside off, Latham lets it be.
Kemar Roach will bowl from the other end. He has three slips and a gully in place. Early wickets is what the Windies need, can he produce it?
Just ahead of a length on middle, Raval defends it by pressing forward. A tight start by Gabriel, 1 of the first over.
Back of a length on off, Raval defends it onto the ground.
New Zealand score their first run! Latham is off the mark. He taps a length ball around middle towards mid on for a quick single. Gabriel is not happy with that single begin conceded.
On the pads, Tom flicks it to square leg. That was nicely timed but he could not find the gap.
Full ball outside off, Latham defends it towards covers.
JAFFA! What a ball to begin with. Perfect line and length for a left-hand batsman. Gabriel lands it around middle, gets it to angle away from the batsman. Latham tries to keep it out but gets beaten.
